title: Briefcase AI Portfolio now supports many more countries
author: Mindless_Might_9759
selftext:
Stock research has become a noise problem for me. There are earnings, price moves, analyst updates and dozens of news stories around every company, and the hard part isn’t finding information anymore. It’s figuring out what actually matters to the stocks you already own. I built Briefcase to supercharge that research process and cut through the noise.

You add your holdings, then Briefcase pulls together market data and relevant news, cross-references what’s happening against your actual portfolio, and gives you sourced portfolio-level insights. The point isn’t to have an LLM blindly pick stocks or execute trades for you. It’s to have an AI research agent constantly answering the question: what happened, which of my holdings does it affect, and why should I care? If there’s no meaningful catalyst, it says that too.

I shipped a pretty big update today. Briefcase previously supported US and Australian securities. It now supports stocks and ETFs across **47 exchanges**, including London, Toronto, Frankfurt, Paris, Tokyo, Hong Kong, India, Singapore, Korea, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, Dubai, Tel Aviv, Istanbul, Warsaw, Jakarta, Bangkok and Johannesburg. I also added support for the new iPhone Duo layout.

Would be interested to hear how people here are currently using AI for portfolio/news research versus actual trade generation.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the noise problem is real. a headline about a stock that's 2% of the portfolio shouldn't sit above a quiet filing on one that's 30% of it.

does Briefcase weight what it surfaces by position size?

comments.author: Mindless_Might_9759
comments.body:
Yep. That’s exactly the problem I wanted to avoid. Briefcase starts from your actual portfolio, so what it surfaces is evaluated in the context of the holdings rather than treating every ticker equally.

A minor position making noise shouldn’t automatically outrank something materially relevant to a core holding. Position size is part of that portfolio context, alongside the actual catalyst/news significance.
